athlete_of_the_week.stat_line: 31/31-of-34 (91.2%), 428 PASS YDS, 5 PASS TD, 0 INT — plus a school-record 16 consecutive completions
athlete_of_the_week.why: The most efficient volume game of the season anywhere in the FBS: 31-of-34 for 428 and five scores with a school-record 16 straight completions (touchdown connections of 50, 38, and 53 yards to Jesse Legree, two more to TE Eric Olsen), on the road, in a conference opener the Beavers won by 30. The FCS-Mercer transfer now leads the FBS with 1,851 passing yards (1,423 through four games + 428 — reconciles exactly with the NCAA leader board through Oct 3).

runners_up.why: Broke a 10–10 tie almost single-handedly in the homecoming rout of a top-ten team.
Turned a 7–3 halftime deficit into a workhorse road win — 34 carries against an SEC front.

runners_up.stat_line: 30/41, 434 PASS YDS, 3 TD, 1 INT + 1 RUSH TD
runners_up.why: Second-most passing yards in Virginia Tech history (behind Bryan Randall's 504 in 2002) — in a loss, which keeps him off the top slot.
Fifth consecutive 100-yard game — only Mike Haas (2005) and Brandin Cooks (2013) had done it at Oregon State.
